proposals.description:

the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan constitution on the taxable property in the Township of Mansfield be increased by 6.5 mills ($6.50 on each $1,000 of Taxable Value) subject to any applicable Headlee rollback under Article IX, Section 31 of the Michigan constitution for the period of five years, 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030, inclusive, the taxes so raised, to be used exclusively for the reconstruction, improvement, maintenance and repair of county…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall
the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan constitution on the taxable property in the Township of Mansfield be increased by 6.5 mills ($6.50 on each $1,000 of Taxable Value) subject to any applicable Headlee rollback under Article IX, Section 31 of the Michigan constitution for the period of five years, 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030, inclusive, the taxes so raised, to be used exclusively for the reconstruction, improvement, maintenance and repair of county roads within the Township of Mansfield and for no other purpose? This levy would raise an estimated $250,937 in the first year.
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 6.5 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.description: Chapter III, Section 1 of the Village Charter Charter currently provides that the president, six trustees, one clerk, one treasurer and one assessor are elected officers. proposals.ballotLanguage:
Chapter III, Section 1 of the Village Charter Charter currently provides that the president, six trustees, one clerk, one treasurer and one assessor are elected officers. The proposed amendment would remove the Clerk and Treasurer from the list of elected officers so that those positions may instead be appointed. The transition would occur through attrition as current elected terms expire, and no current elected term would be shortened. This amendment would take effect only if Proposition B is approved.
Shall Chapter III, Section 1 of the Village Charter be amended accordingly?
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote adopts the change described in the ballot language.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current rules in place.
proposals.conservativeView: Read the full language carefully. Charter changes are hard to undo; be cautious about proposals that expand government authority, create new boards, or raise spending or borrowing limits.
proposals.progressiveView: Supporters typically argue the change modernizes outdated provisions or improves how local government operates.

proposals.description: The Village Charter currently provides that the Clerk and Treasurer are elected offices, all officers must be Village electors, and the Treasurer may serve no more than two consecutive years. proposals.ballotLanguage:
The Village Charter currently provides that the Clerk and Treasurer are elected offices, all officers must be Village electors, and the Treasurer may serve no more than two consecutive years. This amendment provides for the Clerk and Treasurer to be appointed by the President with Council consent, remove the Treasurer’s term limit, and require only elected officers to be Village electors, allowing non-residents to serve in appointed positions. The change would occur through attrition as elected terms expire. No current term would be shortened. This amendment takes effect only if Proposition A is approved.
Shall the Charter be amended accordingly?
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote adopts the change described in the ballot language.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current rules in place.
proposals.conservativeView: Read the full language carefully. Charter changes are hard to undo; be cautious about proposals that expand government authority, create new boards, or raise spending or borrowing limits.
proposals.progressiveView: Supporters typically argue the change modernizes outdated provisions or improves how local government operates.
